name: Particles assemble a glyph (and break apart)

source.description: Two inspected references (batch 1, 2026-11-26): a drifting particle field converges into a letter, and rings shatter into particle rings when they break.

technique: A field of small particles drifts, then each particle travels to a point sampled from a target glyph or mark, so the shape forms out of dust; reversed, a shape breaks into particles that drift away.
purpose: Show emergence (data becomes an answer, n of 1 from a population) or release (a barrier breaks).
visual_behaviour: Thousands of white dots on black drift as a cloud, then sweep into a large lowercase letter within about 0.7 s, which then becomes text; or a glowing ring bursts into dots that spread and fade.
mechanics: Rasterise the target glyph once to an offscreen canvas and sample filled pixels on a jittered grid (seeded) to get N targets; assign each particle a seeded start position; tween progress p 0 -> 1 with staggered power3.out (stagger by distance), draw on Canvas 2D each frame from p (no simulation state); swap to real text at p = 1. Disperse: reverse with outward velocity and fade.
failure_modes: Font not loaded before sampling gives the fallback glyph's shape
Too few particles leave the glyph unreadable; switch to real text at the end
Particles computed by stepping a simulation instead of from timeline progress break seeking

implementation.approach: Canvas 2D layer driven by a GSAP proxy {p}; positions are pure functions of p and seeded starts; Studio.space.assemble (scatter-assemble) covers the DOM-part variant with few elements.

provenance.observed: A field of white particles on black drifts and converges into a large lowercase 'n', which then becomes the line 'n = 1'.
Each ring that the ball escapes breaks into a ring of particles that spreads outward and fades; the last one bursts behind 'ESCAPED.'
The file-icon mark assembles from scattered markup characters inside an expanding ring (7.53-8.6 s and 26.29-27.4 s).
Particles burst from a point (9.39-9.53 s), drift as a cloud and form a word (10.84 s).
A wall of cards dissolves into small mark-shaped particles (10.14-10.24 s) that drift, then spiral inward (11.70-11.87 s).
The sphere bursts into a particle field (5.66 s) that drifts, then converges into a word in 0.3 s (6.62-6.90 s).
Flow-field lines settle into a striped word (5.6-7.1 s); a particle sphere becomes a torus and breaks into particles (7.8-9.1 s).
Low-poly facets fly in one at a time from off-screen, some spinning, and land on a wireframe brain until the mark is complete (2.55-13.1 s).
Particles form a chapter word over a faint clock dial (10.9-12.4 s).
Dots assemble an envelope (3.2-4.1 s), a share and a link icon (5.2-5.7 s) and a signal icon (6.0-6.4 s) that drift and re-form.
